correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructs the static-walk recursion; the n-round condition forces one deletion per round and eliminates stationary 00/11 types; the deletion-time maximum recurrence forces alternating P/Q types and immediate predecessor links; equivalence-class shared-witness sets force uniquely paired blocks with no extra links. Conversely canonical zigzags have exactly the requested deletion trace. The bijection with permutations and two color choices proves \(2n!\) for all n≥1. The same-equivalence case is idempotent after one round. Embedded checker exhaustively tests 145796 models in defined finite domains and an additional 3840 equal-agent models. Enumeration is corroboration, not infinite proof. No missing mathematical lemma is assumed.

value.rationale: This fixed modal formula is a basic two-agent mutual-witness assertion, whose repeated truthful announcements induce a natural finite survival operator. Complete extremal rigidity is a motivated structural question: not merely exhibiting a path or restating n-state monotonicity, but classifying every equality case, giving exact \(2n!\) labelled instances and two isomorphism types. The one-agent collapse isolates a structural reason multi-agent epistemic reasoning can support long finite announcement chains. Results are self-contained and use a natural exact invariant with prospective utility for testing optimality and building hard instances; no unproved general theorem is asserted.
